--- title: "[StepOneHot]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Expand discrete columns into *k* binary indicator columns. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_one_hot.py#L75-L248){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepOneHot(columns, name_fn=None, keep_original_cols=False, id=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each selected column is replaced by *k* indicator columns where *k* is the number of unique non-null levels seen during ``fit()``. Indicators are ``nw.Int8`` (0/1); a column that contains null-source or unseen-level rows is ``nw.Float64`` instead (0.0/1.0/NaN), since pandas' ``Int8`` cannot hold the missing values. Unlike `StepDummy`, no reference level is dropped. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Selector]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns to expand. Accepts a single column name, a list of names, a shoez selector such as ``Selectors.nominal_predictors()`` (see `Selectors` for the full set), or a narwhals or polars selector (``narwhals.selectors.string()``, ``polars.selectors.string()``). Selectors are resolved against the frame's schema when the recipe is fitted, so the same selector works on any backend. Only discrete columns are meaningful here. [name_fn]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Callable[[str, str], str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Callable mapping ``(source_column, level_as_str)`` to the indicator column's name. Default ``None``, which names them ``"{column}_{level}"``. [keep_original_cols]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If ``True``, the source columns are kept alongside the indicators instead of being dropped. Default ``False``. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"one_hot"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each categorical column is replaced by one indicator per level, with no reference level dropped (contrast `StepDummy`): ::: {#3e829b3a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame({"color": ["red", "green", "blue", "red"]}) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
color
0 red
1 green
2 blue
3 red
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#112ca469 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepOneHot(s.nominal_predictors())) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_one_hot(select(role='predictor', type=(String, Categorical, Enum))) [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` records the levels of each selected column: ::: {#ebe55cb8 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 3 columns — 3 predictors Steps: step_one_hot(color → color_blue, color_green, color_red) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` replaces the column with one indicator per level: ::: {#5993ddcf .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
color_blue color_green color_red
0 0 0 1
1 0 1 0
2 1 0 0
3 0 0 1
``` ::: ::: ``keep_original_cols`` keeps the source column alongside them: ::: {#d061b23b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepOneHot(s.nominal_predictors(), keep_original_cols=True)) fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
color color_blue color_green color_red
0 red 0 0 1
1 green 0 1 0
2 blue 1 0 0
3 red 0 0 1
``` ::: :::
